why:
Refuted on subsystem mismatch — the exact recurring false positive AGENTS.md names ("identically-named symbols in a sibling subsystem"). The quote and the code are both accurate; the mapping between them is not.

(1) QUOTE: verbatim at custom-tools.md:455. But the finding stopped two sentences early. The full line reads: "…You can mix them in the same response. In TypeScript, THE SDK saves audio blocks to disk and Claude receives a text block with the saved file path; in Python, THE SDK drops audio blocks from the tool result and logs a warning. THE SDK converts resource link blocks to a text block containing the link's name, URI, and description." Every conversion the sentence promises is attributed to the Agent SDK acting on a handler's return value.

(2) CODE: confirmed. packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:2138-2166 handles only `text` and `image`/`audio`; `resource`/`resource_link` fall through, and `parts.join('\n') || JSON.stringify(result)` fires the raw-JSON fallback only when zero parts were extracted. `grep -ran resource_link` over packages/ and apps/ (NUL-safe, node_modules excluded) returns nothing repo-wide. One layer down, NessyMcpClient.callTool (packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:478-503) forwards the MCP SDK result untouched, so nothing upstream converts the block first.

(3) SUBSYSTEM — the refutation. custom-tools.md governs IN-PROCESS SDK custom tools (`tool()` + `createSdkMcpServer`) and explicitly routes the other case elsewhere at line 859: "To connect to external MCP servers (filesystem, GitHub, Slack) instead of building your own, see Connect MCP servers." mcp-pool.ts IS that external-MCP client pool — the sibling subsystem the page hands off. The surface this page actually governs in our fork is packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:600-633, where every pool tool is wrapped by the SDK's own `tool()` helper; its handler returns `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text: result.content }] }`. A text-only content array is a permitted use of the documented API — the five block types are options a handler MAY return, not an obligation it must satisfy. And because we ship the Claude Agent SDK unmodified, the resource-link→text conversion the sentence describes is present in our runtime for any handler that does return such a block.

There is also no Claude contract on the other side to diverge from: agent-sdk/mcp.md, the page custom-tools.md defers to for external servers, is 900 lines containing zero occurrences of `resource_link`, "resource block", "content block", "content array" or "audio". Claude publishes no documented rule for how a host reduces an external MCP server's result content blocks, so no Claude doc page is violated by mcp-pool.ts's reducer.

Not one of the nine owner decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3, and not a fork product difference (subscription flows, gateway, rename) — it fails on the doc-mapping, not on either of those.

Residual, offered as an observation rather than a finding: the underlying behaviour is real. An external MCP server returning a text block alongside an embedded `resource` block loses the `resource.text`/`resource.blob` payload, because the non-empty `parts` array suppresses the JSON.stringify fallback. If anyone wants to file that, the contract source is the MCP specification's EmbeddedResource/ResourceLink content types, not agent-sdk/custom-tools.md — and it must be scoped to the MCP client pool, naming both backends (Pi and Claude share the pool), not to the SDK custom-tool surface.
correctedState:
The Claude Agent SDK's own handling of `resource` and `resource_link` blocks — the behaviour custom-tools.md:455 actually specifies — is present in this fork, because the SDK ships unmodified and packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:600-633 registers MCP source tools through the SDK's `tool()` + `createSdkMcpServer` helpers. Those handlers return a single `text` block, which the page permits; the five block types are options for a handler, not requirements on it.

Separately, and outside what that page governs: packages/shared/src/mcp/mcp-pool.ts:2138-2166 — the external-MCP client pool's result reducer, shared by the Pi and Claude backends — extracts only `text`, `image` and `audio` blocks from an upstream server's result. A `resource` block's `resource.text`/`resource.blob` payload and a `resource_link` block are skipped, so when the same result also carries a text block the resource payload is dropped (the `JSON.stringify(result)` fallback at :2166 fires only when `parts` is empty, i.e. a resource-only result does survive as raw JSON). `resource_link` appears nowhere in the repo. Nothing upstream converts these blocks first: NessyMcpClient.callTool (packages/shared/src/mcp/client.ts:478-503) forwards the MCP SDK result untouched. No Claude Code doc page specifies this reduction — agent-sdk/mcp.md, the page custom-tools.md defers to for external servers, does not mention content-block types at all — so this is a gap against the MCP specification, not a Claude-docs divergence.
